findings.reason: without an extended legacy form and the pre-merge sidecar census, the definition change orphans every stored review and triggers the fleet-wide re-review wave already measured once (37 sidecars flipped, ~44 reviews composed), which is the failure this section exists to stop.
findings.text: §16 changes the whole-document fingerprint definition to the digest of a sorted section set and has the gate and sweep ask per-section coverage, but a stored record carries only the old whole-document `plan_fingerprint` and no section digests, so every existing review reads as uncovered and earns a fresh one; the plan names neither the legacy/current form mechanism (`_fingerprint_forms`/`plan_fingerprint(legacy=True)`) that §14 and §15 built for exactly this change, nor the sidecar census the s8 correction (comment c-20261004-s8-correction) mandates before a fingerprint-definition change merges

findings.reason: the plan must name the section-extent recognisers to reuse so a section's digest covers exactly the span the landing machinery rewrites, otherwise §16's own done-when (a collapsed section stays covered) can fail on an extent mismatch.
findings.text: §16 has `_authored_prose` "yield one digest per authored section" but names no owner for section extent, while `reckon/_store.py` already owns it through `landed_section_ids`/`_section_heading` — the same span a landing collapse replaces — so a per-section prose walk can segment on boundaries that disagree with the collapse's and cover the wrong span

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §16 hides section identity and per-section coverage behind the existing `plan_fingerprint`/`_authored_prose` pair plus one coverage predicate, rather than a spread of per-section wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16 introduces a second whole-document fingerprint identity without extending the legacy/current fingerprint-form mechanism it would orphan.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1475, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 names the one public definition it adds (the coverage predicate), names why nothing is retired ("the identity digest and the prose walk keep their names and gain a mode"), and reuses the existing plan-review-missing refusal family rather than adding one.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §16 adds a per-authored-section digest but cites no owner for where a section begins and ends, so the new prose walk may re-derive the section extent that `reckon/_store.py` already owns.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §16 states the interface it hides behind and justifies extending the prose-digest owner rather than adding a second walker over the same document.
